patch.value: Prove that a write arriving from another surface reaches a connected subscriber

pm-web, pm-gpt and the pm-mcp endpoint mount the same host directory, so an item edited through one surface is a plain filesystem write as far as the others are concerned. That shared mount establishes storage topology. It does not establish delivery, and nothing asserted delivery.

The pieces were each well covered and the SEAM BETWEEN THEM was not. createProjectWatchCycle resolves its sink as 'deps.emit ?? deliverProjectEvent', and all twelve existing watcher tests inject deps.emit - so the default binding, the only one production uses, was never executed by any test. Renaming or rebinding it would have left the entire suite green while the hosted service silently stopped delivering.

Four cases now drive the real cycle against a real directory, without injecting emit, and read what a real subscriber's response object receives: an out-of-band write is delivered with source filesystem; a first observation baselines rather than announcing a change that did not happen; a subscriber on a different project is NOT told, because a hosted service that broadcast every change to every subscriber would leak the existence and timing of one tenant's edits to another; and delivery through the default sink also records the mutation signal, which is what stops the next tick re-announcing a change this process already made.

Proven not vacuous against two defects. Replacing the default sink with a no-op fails 2 of 4. Making delivery unscoped, so every subscriber receives every project's events, fails the isolation case.
The default emit binding is executed by a test, not only injected around; An out-of-band filesystem write is observed arriving at a subscriber; A subscriber on another project does not receive it

author: claude

value.text:
Greptile: the fourth case asserted consumeSignaledMutation(projectId) returned undefined. That function returns undefined whether or not a signal exists, so removing noteSignaledMutation from deliverProjectEvent left the case green. It proved nothing.

That is the exact failure this suite was written to avoid, in the suite written to avoid it.

Replaced with both halves made observable. That the signal is SET: wasSignaledWithin is false before delivery, true after, and false again once consumed. And that it does the job it exists for: a change this process delivered is not re-announced by the next filesystem sweep, because the watcher suppresses an emit for a signaled project.

Proven: removing noteSignaledMutation from the sink now fails 2 of 5 cases. Against the previous version it failed none.

message: the signal assertion was vacuous; replaced with an observable one
